author: Marshall; Vogel
name_in_asr: Kusinara, Kusinagara; Sarnath (Deer Park); Chaukhandi stupa; Mount Banj
asr_identification: Kasia, Matha Kuar ka Kot (Gorakhpur district) kept for Kusinara against V. A. Smith's Nepal Tarai site, but left open; Chaukhandi stupa = the great stupa 2-3 li SW of the Deer Park monastery; Mount Banj (Mahaban range, Buner) = sanctuary of the body-offering (Stein)
evidence: Vogel's first Kasia season (Nov 1904-Feb 1905): Kusana-period temple under the Nirvana temple, 5th-c. inscribed terracotta Buddha, stupa c. 90 ft square E of the temple, Mauryan chamber, monastery 150 ft square, 5th-c. copper disc; no pillar on the eastern mound (Carlleyle's site for Xuanzang's pillar not confirmed); Sarnath: excavated column c. 50 ft vs Xuanzang's 70 ft, Jagat Singh stupa of brick not stone, main shrine late (9th-c. inscriptions in its foundations); Chaukhandi 800 yds SW of the monastery; Stein's survey of Mount Banj (ruins, red soil)
quote: Whether it will prove to be Kusinara or not, must be left for further excavation to decide…The identification of the Chaukhandi stupa with the vast and splendid memorial which Hiuen Thsang places at two or three A' to the south-west of the Deer Park monastery Is far more convincing…by his finding on Mount Banj the remains of an important Buddhist sanctuary
note: Kasia: Vogel ("I cannot accept Mr. Smith's negative conclusion") keeps Cunningham's Kasia, which Mizutani follows (disputed) and the survey (ASR I) proposed; the excavation itself decides nothing. Marshall doubts Oertel's equations of the Jagat Singh stupa and main shrine with Xuanzang's stone stupa and 200-ft vihara (Mizutani: Dharmarajika = 07.01.03, vihara = Mulagandhakuti). Chaukhandi agrees with Mizutani and ASR I. Mount Banj agrees with Mizutani for 03.04.05 and overturns Cunningham's Manikyala (ASR II).

author: Oertel
name_in_asr: Mrgadava, Deer-park; Dhamek; Bodhisattva stupa; Asoka column
asr_identification: Sarnath = Deer Park; Dhamek tower = the Bodhisattva (Maitreya) stupa (Dharmeksa of the Jain Tirthakalpa); excavated Asoka column = the pillar seen by Xuanzang
evidence: Jinaprabhasuri's Tirthakalpa (1612) names the place near Benares Dharmeksa with a Bodhisattva sanctuary; Asoka column dug to its foot 17 ft below the concrete terrace: shaft c. 27 ft, total c. 37 ft above ground, polished above ground, lion capital and wheel
quote: one cannot hut connect with this the word Dhamek, the current name for the building which ^ suggest may be identified with the Bodhisattva stupa…Hiuen Thsang gives the height of the column seen by him as 70', but, as has already been noticed, his estimates of height cannot be relied upon.
note: Dhamek = Maitreya stupa agrees with Mizutani (07.01.04); first argued here from the Dharmeksa name (Venis); Marshall (P6) doubts it. Column = Xuanzang's pillar agrees with Mizutani for 07.01.03. Not in the Cunningham-series ASR column (Cunningham took Dhamek for Asoka's relic stupa).

author: Oertel
asr_identification: Dhamek = memorial where Maitreya received the prediction; Chaukhandi stupa = Xuanzang's 300-ft stupa 2-3 li SW of the convent (where the five ascetics met the Buddha)
evidence: Dhamek: solid stone to 36 ft 9 in, Cunningham's 1835 shaft found no relics; main niche faces W; Chaukhandi excavated: three square terraces c. 12 ft high and broad on a concrete floor, octagonal plinth above, matching the "three robes, inverted bowl, staff" stupa form; estimated height c. 200 ft
quote: It seems more likely, however, that the Dhamek tower was a memorial erected on the spot where Maitreya received an assurance from Sakyamuni that he would be the next Buddha…This is the stupa which there seems good reason for identifying with the Chaukhapdl, though this latter structure contains niches in the terrace walls.
note: Both agree with Mizutani (07.01.04 Dhamekh; 07.01.10 Chaukhandi) and Chaukhandi with Cunningham (ASR I); the excavation adds the terraced plan, though Xuanzang says the stupa had no niches. Marshall's footnote doubts relics in a memorial stupa.

author: Oertel; Vogel
asr_identification: Sarnath monastery = the Saddharmacakra (Dharmacakra) convent of the Deer Park
evidence: monastic clay seal (5th-6th c.) with wheel-and-deer symbol and legend "Sri sad-dharmma[cakre] bhiksusanghasya", read on the analogy of the Kasia monastery seals; Guptasimha private seal
quote: would seem to belong not to a private individual but to a monastic establishment. It is of the same type as the vihara seals found at Kasia…The word dharmacakra is supplied by the Mahipala inscription.
note: Epigraphic confirmation of Sarnath = Deer Park (Mizutani 07.01.02a; ASR I Cunningham), which was not in doubt; see P68 for the fuller seals of 1906-07.
Epigraphy summary (Mahaban: no inscriptions; Sarnath, Kasia inscriptions); no location.

author: Konow
asr_identification: Cola kingdom known from inscriptions of the Cuddapah district (before the 8th c.)
evidence: inscriptions from the Cuddapah district of an independent early Cola dynasty (Venkayya)
quote: Several inscriptions from the Cuddapah district contain information of a dynasty of Colas, which has not formerly been noticed…Mr. Venkayya draws attention to the fact that this Cola Kingdom might well correspond to Hiuen Thsang’s description of Chu-li-ye.
note: Konow summarising Venkayya. Puts Culya in the Cuddapah district (upper Pennar basin), near but not identical with Mizutani's Pennar basin with capital Nellore; nothing in the survey (ASR) column. See P51 (Venkayya 1905-06).

author: Marshall
name_in_asr: Kasia; Kusinara ("Great Decease" monastery); Kusagarapura; Rajagrha; Sattapanni Hall; Bamboo Garden
asr_identification: identity of Kasia with Kusinara left open; the Rajgir survey settles the Sattapanni Hall and Bamboo Garden (see P41)
evidence: Vogel's 1905-06 season at Kasia: sangharama wall c. 5,000 ft enclosing c. 36 acres, earlier monastery L burnt c. end of 5th c. (dated by sealings), numerous sealings of the monastery of the "Great Decease"; Rajgir: survey of c. 35 sq. miles, trial pits in New Rajagrha, Hindu (Gupta) tower in the old city
quote: The question of the identity of this sacred site still remains •open, though some evidence on the point may perhaps be deduced from the discovery •of numerous seals, emanating from the monastery of the "Great Decease.”…it may be inferred, therefore, that Kasla is not the spot where Buddha attained his nirvana.
note: Marshall reads the letter-seals as evidence against Kasia = Kusinara (Mizutani: Kasia, disputed; survey: Kasia, Cunningham ASR I), while leaving open Vogel's hypothesis that the Kasia convent was affiliated to the Great Decease monastery. Rajgir details in P41.

author: Vogel; Marshall
name_in_asr: Kusinara; Mahaparinirvana convent; Makuta-bandhana; Kusmara (Anrudhva); Kusagarapura
asr_identification: Kasia remains: their identity with Kusinara undecided (seals of the Mahaparinirvana convent may be imported letter-seals); town of Kusinara, if Kasia, between Anrudhva and Sisva, not at Anrudhva; Old Rajagrha outer walls = Xuanzang's 150-li circuit
evidence: clay seals (c. 400-900 AD) of the "Mahaparinirvana-vihara" with Buddha's coffin between twin sal trees; two seals (c. 400 and c. 600 AD) of the Makuta-bandhana (cremation) convent; Anrudhva digs found religious buildings (32-ft plinth, three small stupas), no town; Marshall's Rajgir survey: outer walls along the hills to Giriak match 150 li at 6 li to the mile, inner city walls c. 4 miles
quote: In the former case, the}^ prove the remains near Kasia to represent the great sanctuary of Kusinara, in the other case they prove the…These two belong to the convent of Makuta-bandhana which, as we know, was the place where Buddha’s remains were cremated…we find that the distance covered by the walls agrees remarkably well with the 150 li of Hiuen Thsang
note: Vogel withdraws his earlier view that the seals prove Kasia = Kusinara; Mizutani's Kasia (06.04, 06.04.03) and the survey's (Cunningham ASR I: city = Anrudhwa) are left unproved; Vogel shows Anrudhwa is not the town. Rajgir: Marshall rejects Cunningham's emendation of 150 li to 50 li (ASR I/III); agrees with Mizutani's Old Rajagrha (09.02.04).

author: Marshall
name_in_asr: Grdhrakuta; Pippala stone house; Bamboo Garden (Venuvana); Karanda tank; stupa of Ajatasatru; Sattapanni Hall
asr_identification: Grdhrakuta = Chhatha-giri (not Saila-giri); Pippala stone house = stone watch-tower above the hot springs on Vaibhara; Bamboo Garden = gardens N of the old N gate, vihara probably under the mound with a Muslim saint's grave; Karanda tank = deep ancient tank N of it; Ajatasatru stupa possibly a plinth at the foot of Vipula behind the Suraj Kund; Sattapanni Hall = artificially levelled spur on the N face of Vaibhara c. 1 mile W of the Pippala house
evidence: survey and climbing of Chhatha-giri: Bimbisara's causeway from Udaya-giri, the two small stupas (Hia-Shing, T'ui-fan) still on it, excavated (10th-12th-c. fragments), brick vihara ruins on the W precipice and a stupa below; Bloch's trenches in the garden mound: nine brick stupas on a concrete floor, creed tablets 10th-11th c.; Sattapanni spur: pebble-paved terrace, ramps, cyclopean walls; Cunningham's Son Bhandar and Stein's Adinatha caves rejected; Cunningham's mound H for the Asoka stupa trenched (Mauryan bricks reused under a Jaina statue)
quote: That hill is Chhatha-giri, which rises up in a solitary conic.il peak (Plate XXXII) beriveen Ratna-giri and Saila-giri…This tank there is every reason to ideniifv with the Karanda-hrada…at a distance of a little over a mile — corresponding to the 5 or 6 li of the Chinese travellers — the hill puts out a small spur
note: Revises Cunningham (Grdhrakuta = Saila-giri; Sattapanni = Son Bhandar, ASR I/III) and Stein. Grdhrakuta, Pippala house, Venuvana and Karanda tank agree with Mizutani; the Sattapanni Hall as a structural hall on a spur, not a cave, differs from Mizutani's "Saptaparna cave on Baibhara"; Ajatasatru's stupa at the foot of Vipula differs from Mizutani's mound on the E side of the road (uncertain).
Amaravati excavation (Rea) and caves; no Xuanzang location argued.
Jaina images, Burmese pagodas; no location.

author: Konow
asr_identification: Kasia is not Kusinara: its monastery received letters from the Kusinara monastery
evidence: clay seals of the Mahaparinirvana monastery from Vogel's Kasia excavation, read as letter-seals sent from Kusinara
quote: and their number is great enough to warrant the conclusion that the Kasia monastery was in close contact with that of Kusinara. The seals have apparentl]^ been attached to letters sent b}^ the friars of Kusinara to their brethren in Kasia
note: Konow (epigraphy summary 1905-06) takes the seals against Mizutani's and the survey's (Cunningham ASR I) Kasia; same evidence as P39-40, later overturned by the Kasia finds of 1910-11 (not in this batch).

author: Venkayya
asr_identification: Kurnool district: a Telugu Cola kingdom in S Kurnool, N Cuddapah and SW Anantapur
evidence: Cola inscriptions in N Cuddapah (kings claiming descent from Karikala) and round Hemavati (Anantapur), 8th c.; bearing SW of Dhanyakataka (Amaravati)
quote: Chu-li-ye was south-west of Dhanyakataka, the old name of Amaravati in the Guntur district…This description of Chudi-y^e takes us to the Kumool district for its location…there was a Co]a kingdom comprising perhaps the southern portion of the Kumool district, the northern part of Cuddappah
note: Differs from Mizutani (Pennar basin, capital Nellore) by putting Culya inland in Kurnool/Cuddapah; agrees that Culya is not the Tamil Cola country. Nothing in the survey (ASR) column.

author: Marshall; Vogel
asr_identification: Kasia remains = Vethadipa (Vishnudvipa), one of the eight relic-stupa places, not Kusinara (tentative)
evidence: 1906-07 season: c. 500 clay sealings, 464 of the "Convent of the Great Decease", 9 of other convents; baked-clay seal-die "Sri-Vishnudvipa-vihare bhikshu-sanghasya" found 19 ft 6 in E of monastery O, 3 ft 6 in deep; monastery doors facing E as in Xuanzang's description; Ramabhar and the Matha-Kuar stupa still unexcavated
quote: As I will endeavour to show, it renders it highly probable that these remains represent not Kusinara, but V ethadipa, another of the eight places at which a portion of Buddha’s relics was presented…It would be hazardous to consider the identification as proved by a small object of portable size
note: Vogel now moves Kasia away from Kusinara, against Mizutani's Kasia (06.04, 06.04.03) and the survey's (Cunningham ASR I); Marshall: "we cannot look upon the question as settled". Vethadipa is not a Xiyu ji place. The view was later abandoned (Kasia finds of 1910-11, later reports). Also covers the start of the 1906-07 Sarnath report (gandhakuti seals; see P68).
Sarnath building descriptions (bricks, walls); no identification.

author: Konow; Marshall
asr_identification: Sarnath monastery = Saddharmachakra; Mulagandhakuti (perhaps the shrine of the colossal statue seen by Xuanzang) to be sought E of the Main Shrine; Dharmarajika of the Mahipala inscription = Asoka's stupa; Dhamekh < dharmeksha
evidence: seals with wheel-and-deer and legend "Sri-saddharmachakre mulagandhakutyam bhagavatah" (6th-7th c.) found W of the main shrine; lamp-posts inscribed for the mulagandhakuti found E of the main shrine; 11th-c. inscription naming the Saddharmachakrapravartana-vihara; Spooner (Sahri-Bahlol): neither Sahri-Bahlol nor Takht-i-Bahi is mentioned by the pilgrims
quote: These seals thus furnish us with the name of the old Sarnath monastery…The Mnlagandhakutl must, then, be the principal gandhakutl, perhaps the place where the colossal statue seen by Hiuen Thsang was put up…Dhamekh therefore regularly corresponds to an older dharmeksha
note: Inscriptional basis for Mizutani's "200-ft vihara = Mulagandhakuti" (07.01.02a); Konow places it E of the Main Shrine rather than in it. Dharmarajika = Asoka stupa supports Mizutani's 07.01.03 (Jagat Singh stupa); dharmeksha supports Oertel (P7) on Dhamekh. Not in the survey (ASR) column.
Gandhara iconography; Bloch on the Lauriya funeral mounds (not a Xiyu ji place).

author: Vogel
asr_identification: ancient Mathura = the extensive elevated ground SW of the modern town, not the Katra; Upagupta monastery and monkey tank still unlocated
evidence: review of past finds (Katra = Yasa-vihara still extant mid-6th c., Kankali Tila Jaina stupa); Kesopura named after the Kesava Dev temple, not Arrian's Klisobora
quote: The attempts made by Cunningham and Growse to identify some of the Mathura sites with localities mentioned by Hiuen Tsiang have signally failed…the site of ancient Mathura is clearly indicated by an extensive elevation of the soil to, the south-west of the town…both the Upagupta monaster}- and the monkey tank are still to be discovered.
note: Rejects the survey's Katra = Upagupta monastery and Jail mound = monkey tank (Cunningham ASR I, III) and Cunningham's emendations of Xuanzang; agrees with Mizutani that 04.07.03 cannot be located; capital of 04.07 placed SW of the town.

author: Sahni
asr_identification: Fleet's Kusinara near Pachrukhi (Saran) and Anoma crossing near Majhauli (Gorakhpur): no supporting remains found
evidence: tour of Nov-Dec 1906 through Fleet's list of c. 50 places; village Anuaurpari ("across the Anuma") 4 miles from Majhauli, but no stream of that name (channel called Pusi) and no Buddhist remains
quote: As regards the suggested location of Kusin.irfi near Pachrukhi and cf the spot where Gautama crossed the Anoma, which Dr. Fleet had been inclined to locate somewhere in the vicinity of Majhauli…the results of m3' short tour must be regarded as rather of negative than positive vaiue.
note: Negative fieldwork on Fleet's alternatives; leaves Mizutani's Kasia (06.04) and his uncertain Anoma (06.03.03) untouched; survey column: Anoma = Kudawa Nala (Carlleyle).
Khaira, Don Buzurg, Titira (Sahni); no Xiyu ji place.

author: Sahni
asr_identification: Fleet's proposed Kusinara near Pachrukkhi (Saran district): no antiquities found
evidence: search of several villages round Pachrukkhi railway station: no remains
quote: it is somewhere in the neighbourliood of this village that Dr. Fleet is inclined to locate the scene of Buddha’s faritntvaiia. I carcfullv searched several villages round Pachrukkhi for any antiquities that might be still extant, but in vain.
note: Negative result for Fleet's alternative to Kasia; nothing against Mizutani's Kasia or the survey's.
Xuanzang quoted on the religions of Dravida; no location argued (see P96).
Xuanzang quoted on the people of Dravida; no location argued.

author: Venkayya
asr_identification: Dravida = the Pallava country (later Tondai-mandalam), capital Kanci
quote: The Chinese pilgrim Htuen Isnng c.ills this tract cf country Ta-lo pi-ch’a or Drutida — not lomlainltu or Tondai-manilalani as it was known in later times
note: Agrees with Mizutani (Dravida, capital Kancipura = Conjeeveram). No fieldwork. Nothing in the survey (ASR) column.
